This is Digital Realty facility AUS11, at 7500 Metro Center Drive, Austin, TX 78744. Digital Realty's own property listing confirms this address as AUS11, but this session's fetch did not return a confirmed square footage figure for it specifically.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is Digital Realty's Austin-metro property, a smaller footprint than its Dallas-Fort Worth cluster also tracked in this registry. Austin has drawn substantial hyperscale and enterprise data center investment in recent years, served primarily by Austin Energy within city limits and Oncor Electric Delivery in surrounding Travis County areas. Digital Realty markets its Austin property under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning it alongside the company's larger Texas footprint in Dallas-Fort Worth, also tracked in this registry, within its global interconnection and colocation platform.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage; the company reports its portfolio metrics by region and metro rather than disclosing per-building IT power ratings for any of its facilities, a pattern consistent across every Digital Realty property researched this session, not specific to this building alone.

reading.body:
Digital Realty's Austin facility AUS11 occupies 85,500 square feet across two stories at 7500 Metro Center Drive but publishes no IT power capacity figure for this building. The operator discloses facility counts and regional square footage in its SEC filings rather than per-building megawatt ratings, a consistent practice across its entire US portfolio of 118 data centers. This property holds SOC2, SOC3, and PCI-DSS certifications, qualifies for CEEDA Gold status, and reports 100% renewable energy sourcing, characteristics matching colocation and wholesale hosting use cases rather than constraining the site to a particular tenant class.

Austin has 133 mapped data center facilities statewide, of which 18 publish confirmed megawatt figures totaling 468 megawatts. AUS11 does not appear in the published MW count, placing it outside the ranked tier of disclosed capacity in Texas. The facility represents Digital Realty's single named Austin-metro property, smaller in scale than the company's Dallas-Fort Worth cluster also operating in the state, and sits within Austin Energy's service territory in the city proper.

Because AUS11's IT load is not published, whether this campus matters to AI scaling depends entirely on what tenants lease inside. Digital Realty's landlord model means the power consumed here flows to hyperscalers, enterprises, or other operators, not disclosed at the property level. The 85,500 square feet and colocation certifications indicate capacity for enterprise and mid-scale cloud use, but without megawatt figures or tenant names, the site's role in Texas AI infrastructure cannot be quantified from public sources.
